data.title: Copper Lake Announces Closing of Second and Final Tranche of Previously Announced Non-Brokered Private Placement
data.description:
Toronto, Ontario--(Newsfile Corp. - October 16, 2026) - Copper Lake Resources Ltd. (FSE: W0I0) ("Copper Lake" or the "Company") announces that it has closed the second and final tranche (the "Final Tranche") of its non-brokered private placement (the "Offering") previously announced on September 3, 2026 (the "Private Placement").

Under the final tranche closing of the Offering, the Company issued 17,708,292 units ("Units") at a price of $0.15 per Unit for gross proceeds of $2,656,243. Each Unit consists of one common share and one Warrant. Each Warrant entitles the holder to acquire one additional share at an exercise price of $0.20 per Common Share for a period of 24 months from the closing date.

The Company has raised a total of $4,999,998 and issued 33,333,323 Units in connection with both tranches of the Offering.

The Warrants shall be subject to an accelerated expiry date clause whereby, at any time following the expiry of the four-months and one day hold period, should the weighted average closing price of the Common Shares on the TSX Venture Exchange (the "TSX-V") be more than $0.40 for a period of 15 consecutive trading days, the Company shall be entitled to accelerate the expiry date of the warrants to a date which is 30 days following the date on which the Company announces the accelerated expiry of the Warrants by press release.

The net proceeds of the financing will be used for exploration at the Company's Marshall Lake project and for general working capital purposes.

In accordance with applicable Canadian securities laws, all securities issued pursuant to the private placement will have a hold period of four months and one day from the date of issuance.

Certain insiders of the Company purchased 1,473,333 Units in the Private Placement and such participation is considered to be a "related party transaction" pursuant to Multilateral Instrument 61-101 ("MI 61-101"). The Company intends to rely on the exemptions from the formal valuation and minority shareholder approval requirements of MI 61-101 contained in Section 5.5(a) and Section 5.7(1)(a) of MI 61-101 in respect of such insider participation.

The Private Placement has been conditionally approved by the TSX Venture Exchange, but completion of the private placement remains subject to the receipt of all necessary regulatory approvals, including approval of the TSX-V.

In accordance with applicable Canadian securities laws, all securities issued pursuant to the private placement will have a hold period of four months and one day from the date of issuance.

ABOUT COPPER LAKE RESOURCES

Copper Lake Resources Ltd. is a publicly traded Canadian mineral exploration and development company with interests in two projects both located in Ontario.

The Marshall Lake high-grade VMS copper, zinc, silver and gold project, comprises an area of approximately 220 square km located 120 km north of Geraldton, Ontario and is just 22 km north of the main CNR rail line. Copper Lake has an 82.97% interest in the joint ventured property, which consists of 233 claims and 52 mining leases. The project also includes 148 claim cells staked in 2018 and 2020 that are 100% owned and not subject to any royalties. These newer claims add approximately 30 square km to the property.

In addition to the original Marshall Lake property above, Marshall Lake also includes the Sollas Lake and Summit Lake properties, which are 100% owned by the Company and are not subject to any royalties. The Sollas Lake property consists of 20 claim cells comprising an area of 4 square km on the east side of the Marshall Lake property where historical EM airborne geophysical surveys have outlined strong conductors on the property hosted within the same favorable felsic volcanic units. The Summit Lake property currently consists of 100 claim cells comprising an area of 20.5 square km, is accessible year-round, and is located immediately west of the original Marshall Lake property. The Marshall Lake project is located in the traditional territories of Aroland and Animbiigoo Zaagi'igan Anishinaabek ("AZA") First Nations.

Copper Lake has a 69.79% joint venture interest in the Norton Lake nickel, copper, cobalt, and palladium PGM property, located in the southern Ring of Fire area, is approximately 100 km north of the Marshall Lake Property. The Company filed an updated NI 43-101 in October 2023 with a mineral resource of open pit and underground Measured + Indicated Resources of 1,795,000 tonnes at an average grade of 0.72% NI, 0.69% Cu, 339 ppm Co, 0.52 g/t Pd, 0.17 g/t Pt and containing 28.3Mlbs of nickel and 27.3Mlbs of copper. The Norton Lake property is located in the traditional territories of Eabametoong ("Fort Hope") and Neskantaga First Nations.

data.title: Enova, Grasshopper Bancorp Terminate Merger Deal
data.description:
By Stephen Nakrosis

Enova International and Grasshopper Bancorp have mutually terminated a planned merger, the companies said.

Enova was slated to acquire Grasshopper in a cash-and-stock deal valued at about $369 million under the terms of the deal announced in December. The financial services company would have seen Grasshopper, a full-service digital bank founded in 2019, become a fully owned bank subsidiary. Grasshopper had more than $1.4 billion in total assets as of Sept. 30, 2025, Enova said.

Enova said it paid $4 million to Grasshopper as part of the termination agreement.

data.title: Air Traffic Controllers' Practice of Leaving Work Early Targeted in Pay Deal — WSJ
Yes Bank flags 250-bps impact on core capital ratio after Supreme Court upholds AT-1 bond write-off ruling
data.description:
New Delhi, Oct. 17 -- Yes Bank said its Common Equity Tier 1 (CET1) capital ratio could decline by around 250 basis points, a day after the Supreme Court upheld the Bombay High Court judgment against the write-down of Additional Tier-1 (AT-1) bonds worth Rs.8,415 crore, undertaken in March 2020 as part of the bank's reconstruction.

The bank's overall Tier 1 capital ratio, however, is expected to remain unchanged at 14% on a pro forma basis, the bank said in its exchange filing on Friday. Capital ratios measure a bank's financial strength by comparing its capital with its risk-weighted assets, indicating its ability to withstand losses.

Additional Tier-1 (AT-1) bonds are perpetual instruments issued by banks to increase their capital base. They are riskier than traditional bonds and typically offer higher interest rates. The RBI can require their write-down or cancellation under specified circumstances if a bank is in financial trouble.

The Supreme Court on Thursday dismissed appeals filed by Yes Bank, the Reserve Bank of India (RBI), and the Union government, upholding the Bombay High Court's January 20, 2023, judgment on the matter.

The bank is examining the judgment in detail, including evaluating all available legal options and suitable actions or steps going forward, Yes Bank said in a regulatory filing.

The bank also said it has access to various capital-management levers and retains the flexibility to undertake additional capital actions, as considered appropriate, to pursue its growth objectives.

The bank remains focused on strengthening its franchise and providing consistent service and support to customers across their banking requirements, it added.

Separately, S&P Global Ratings said it does not expect the Supreme Court ruling against Yes Bank to affect its ratings, although it could weigh on future earnings, Reuters reported.

Yes Bank's regulatory capital is adequate, with its Common Equity Tier 1 ratio of 13.87% as of the end of March 2026 able to absorb the expected 250-basis-point hit while remaining well above the minimum requirement of 5.5%, S&P said.

The ratings agency said the lender's credit profile could withstand the ruling, which addresses procedural lapses in the write-down under the 2020 rescue. S&P expects Yes Bank to remain adequately capitalised, with its risk-adjusted capital ratio projected to remain between 8% and 8.5% through March 2028, compared with 9% in March 2026, according to the report.

Following the news, investors grew concerned about the bank's financial health, resulting in a 14% crash in Thursday's trade. The sell-off extended into Friday's session, with the stock falling another 3.42%.

The losses have widened the bank's October losses to 17% so far, while the stock has declined 19% in 2026.

data.title: Tesla Showcases Roadster With SpaceX-Developed Thrusters In Dramatic Aerial Demonstration
data.description:
WASHINGTON (dpa-AFX) - Tesla (TSLA) has showcased its redesigned Roadster performing aerial stunts using rocket-inspired cold-gas thrusters developed with help from SpaceX engineers, offering a new look at the long-delayed electric sports car ahead of its expected 2028 production.

During the October 15 demonstration near Waco, Texas, the two-seat Roadster drove up a curved ramp, briefly remained upside down using a suction system and launched into the air before landing on its wheels. It also performed a jump over several Tesla vehicles.

Tesla showed footage indicating the Roadster accelerating from zero to 60 miles per hour in 0.81 seconds, though the performance has not been independently verified.

The company has not confirmed whether the thrusters and flying capabilities demonstrated by the prototype will appear on the production vehicle.

Final specifications, pricing and delivery details also remain unclear. The next-generation Roadster was originally unveiled in 2017 but has faced repeated production delays.

data.title: Nowhere to hide: Tech selloff hits software and chip stocks alike
data.description:
By Hannah Pedone

The software and semiconductor sectors haven't been trading in tandem much this year, but they collectively fell Friday as AI and interest-rate fears hit the market

Shares of Salesforce closed down 2% on Friday amid a broad-based selloff in the technology stocks.

Even the software sector wasn't immune from a broad-based technology selloff in the stock market Friday.

Investors had been rotating into the software sector earlier in the week, deeming these stocks to be compelling alternatives to highflying chip stocks that were seen as more vulnerable to concerns about the sustainability of artificial-intelligence spending.

But semiconductor and software stocks fell in tandem on Friday, leaving tech investors with nowhere to hide. The iShares Expanded Tech-Software Sector exchange-traded fund IGV, a proxy for the software sector, closed down 4.8%, while the iShares Semiconductor ETF SOXX was off 4.1%.

Within the software sector, ServiceNow's stock (NOW) finished down 4% and Oracle's stock (ORCL) closed 5% lower. Shares of Salesforce (CRM) lost 2% on the day, while Twilio's stock (TWLO) was the S&P 500's SPX biggest loser with its 10.6% decline.

D.A. Davidson analyst Gil Luria told MarketWatch that what used to be a negative correlation between chip stocks and software stocks is "no longer a major factor in the market." He said that Friday's broad-based technology selloff was "not leaving any stock untouched."

"Investors no longer view AI progress as bad for software and are treating individual software companies based on their specific prospects," he said.

Morningstar analyst Luke Yang told MarketWatch there wasn't one single factor gripping the market on Friday, as investors seemed to be digesting a broad breakdown of faith in the AI trade this week.

The "wide range of potential outcomes" for companies tied to the AI trade has made it difficult for investors to maintain faith in AI-exposed stocks, he said - whether it be the indebted neocloud provider CoreWeave (CRWV), chip giant like Nvidia (NVDA) or software and cloud company Oracle (ORCL).

Cybersecurity stocks were also caught up in the software selloff on Friday after Palo Alto Networks (PANW) - which sells firewall products to corporate customers - released an advisory disclosing a security vulnerability earlier this week. The Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency, which lies within the U.S. Department of Homeland Security, added Palo Alto Networks to its catalog of known security vulnerabilities.

The Amplify Cybersecurity ETF HACK closed down 4% on Friday, with Palo Alto Networks and CrowdStrike Holdings (CRWD) shares each falling more than 7%.

One issue could be the specter of interest-rate hikes, which affects technology companies across the board that have to borrow money.

The "data-center buildout requires capital which is becoming more expensive," Luria said, as higher rates mean higher funding costs for companies investing heavily in AI infrastructure.

Software stocks are also sensitive to rate hikes as their valuations are often tied to cash flows years into the future, and higher interest rates change the way those are valued. And many software companies need to borrow money as well.

Financial-technology stocks may be feeling the pain as well from fears of an imminent rate hike, as higher rates mean higher default risk for lenders, Mizuho anlayst Dan Dolev told MarketWatch.

Speaking Friday at the International Monetary Fund and World Bank Group's annual meeting in Bangkok, Federal Reserve Chairman Kevin Warsh declined to share any expectations for the central bank's upcoming rate-setting meeting.

-Hannah Pedone

This content was created by MarketWatch, which is operated by Dow Jones & Co. MarketWatch is published independently from Dow Jones Newswires and The Wall Street Journal.

data.title: Character.ai Files For Chapter 11 Bankruptcy
data.description:
WASHINGTON (dpa-AFX) - Artificial intelligence chatbot startup Character.ai has filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy and plans to pursue a court-supervised sale by the end of the year as it faces mounting legal, regulatory and operational pressures.

Disney has emerged as a potential bidder, agreeing to pay $20 million for certain Character.ai intellectual property and provide transition services through former employees it has hired. The arrangement is expected to help keep the chatbot platform operating during the bankruptcy process.

Founded in 2021 by former Google researchers Noam Shazeer and Daniel de Freitas, Character.ai previously reached a $1 billion valuation following a $150 million funding round. Its bankruptcy filing lists assets of between $50 million and $100 million.

The company has faced several lawsuits alleging its chatbots contributed to suicide, self-harm and other harms involving teenagers.

Character.ai settled five cases earlier this year and introduced additional safety measures, including restricting users under 18 from engaging in back-and-forth chatbot conversations. The company said it could wind down the platform if a sale is not completed.

data.title: Moody's upgrades Egypt by a notch as structural reforms bolster economic resilience
data.description:
Moody's upgraded Egypt's long-term sovereign credit rating by one notch to "B3" from "Caa1" on Friday, citing strong fiscal consolidation and structural reforms.

"The shift to a flexible exchange rate and tighter monetary policy has strengthened external buffers and the economy's capacity to absorb shocks," the global credit ratings agency said in a statement. It maintained the country's outlook at "positive".

The International Monetary Fund said on Thursday Egypt has made good progress in restoring macroeconomic stability despite external challenges, however, it must speed up structural reforms to reduce the state's footprint in the economy.

The North African country, which is preparing for the final review of $8 billion in IMF loans in the coming weeks, has indicated it would not seek further IMF financing after the facility expires in December.

"The government's ability to sustain this credit-positive trend despite a challenging external environment and higher oil prices highlights the durability of the improvement, rooted in increased policy effectiveness," Moody's said.

Egypt's economy grew 5.1% in the 2025-26 financial year, compared with 4.4% in the previous year, according to a cabinet statement last month.

Peer agencies S&P and Fitch last week affirmed their ratings on Egypt with a "stable" outlook.

data.title: Court backs EPA giving Oklahoma authority over environmental rules on tribal lands
data.description:
Key points:
  • 10th Circuit says EPA had authority under 2005 law to approve Oklahoma's authority
  • EPA had shifted positions during Trump and Biden administrations
  • Dissent says EPA had discretion to impose at least some protections for tribal interests

By Nate Raymond

A divided federal appeals court on Friday upheld a Trump administration decision to unconditionally grant Oklahoma authority over environmental programs on tribal lands within the state.

A 2-1 panel of the Denver-based 10th US Circuit Court of Appeals ruled that the US Environmental Protection Agency acted in accordance with a long-dormant provision in a 2005 transportation funding bill that allows Oklahoma to seek authority over environmental regulatory programs in Native American territory.

The provision was dubbed the "Midnight Rider" because it was added late and without discussion to the Safe, Accountable, Flexible, Efficient Transportation Equity Act.

Oklahoma did not invoke the provision until 2020, after the US Supreme Court's 5-4 decision in McGirt v. Oklahoma, which recognized about half of Oklahoma — much of the eastern part of the state — as Native American reservation land beyond the jurisdiction of state authorities.

Later that year, the EPA during President Donald Trump’s first administration approved Oklahoma’s request.

At the request of several tribes including the Pawnee Nation, the EPA under Democratic President Joe Biden withdrew the approval in 2021 and reconsidered the matter. In Biden's final days in office, the EPA again approved Oklahoma's request but with a condition that the state engage in efforts to seek consensus with affected tribes.

But once Trump returned to the White House, the agency issued a new decision last year eliminating that condition, prompting a lawsuit by the Pawnee Nation.

The tribe argued the EPA’s action violated the Administrative Procedure Act, saying the Midnight Rider expired in 2009 along with other parts of the 2005 spending law and that EPA wrongly concluded under Trump that it had no authority to impose conditions when approving Oklahoma's request.

But US Circuit Judge Timothy Tymkovich, writing for the majority, said the Midnight Rider contained no sunset provision and did not authorize the Biden-era condition.

"Congress’s command that the EPA 'shall approve' a valid request does not authorize the agency to shrink that approval by attaching a condition to it," he wrote.

Michael Freeman, a lawyer for Pawnee Nation at Earthjustice, called the ruling disappointing and said his client was considering its options.

Tymkovich, who was appointed by Republican President George W. Bush, was joined by US Circuit Judge Robert Bacharach, an appointee of Democratic President Barack Obama.

US Circuit Judge Richard Federico, a Biden appointee, dissented, saying the EPA had the discretion to impose at least some protections for tribal interests.

"This court should not so readily acquiesce to the total displacement of the tribes as the first sovereigns of their land absent a clear statement from Congress to the contrary," he wrote.

The case is Pawnee Nation of Oklahoma v Zeldin, 10th US Circuit Court of Appeals, No. 25-9548.

For Pawnee Nation of Oklahoma: Michael Freeman of Earthjustice

For the United States: Cameron Hinojos of the US Department of Justice

EPA withdraws Trump Oklahoma environment order after input from tribes

Tribes slam EPA move to give Oklahoma control of environmental rules

data.title: Novartis Discontinues Mid-Stage Lupus Trial In Latest Pipeline Setback
data.description:
Key points:
  • Iptacopan is sold under the brand name Fabhalta and is approved by the FDA for Paroxysmal Nocturnal Hemoglobinuria, Primary Immunoglobulin A Nephropathy, and C3 Glomerulopathy.
  • Novartis has faced multiple clinical setbacks over the past several weeks, including trial failures and development discontinuations.
  • According to data from Koyfin, 8 of the 23 analysts rate the stock a ‘buy’ or ‘strong buy,’ while 13 rate it a ‘hold’ and only two rate it ‘sell.’

Shares of Novartis (NVS) closed little changed on Friday after the company decided to discontinue its mid-stage trial of iptacopan in lupus nephritis.

According to a federal clinical trials registry update, the company has concluded the study over ‘strategic considerations.’ It is unclear if the discontinuation was spurred by efficacy or safety concerns.

The multi-location study aimed to evaluate the efficacy, safety, and tolerability of iptacopan (LNP023) in addition to standard-of-care treatment. The company decided to conclude the study after completing the first part, as per the database.

Iptacopan is sold under the brand name Fabhalta and is approved by the FDA for Paroxysmal Nocturnal Hemoglobinuria, Primary Immunoglobulin A Nephropathy, and C3 Glomerulopathy.

Latest Pipeline Setback For Novartis

Novartis has faced multiple clinical setbacks over the past several weeks. Last month, the company said that its late-stage trial of Pelacarsen, being developed as a treatment to lower elevated lipoprotein(a) or Lp(a) and reduce the risk of major cardiovascular events, missed its primary goal. The company also said that its late-stage trial of del-desiran in myotonic dystrophy type 1 (DM1) missed its primary endpoint.

Besides the late-stage drug failures, the company also discontinued development of VHB937 in mid-September after a mid-stage study missed primary and secondary goals. Prior to that, in August, Novartis paused multiple autoimmune and neurology trials after three fatal cases of immune effector cell-associated hemophagocytic syndrome (IEC-HS) in patients taking its experimental therapy Rap-cel.

According to data from Koyfin, 8 of the 23 analysts rate the stock a ‘buy’ or ‘strong buy,’ while 13 rate it a ‘hold’ and only two rate it ‘sell.’

How Did NVS Retail Traders React?

On Stocktwits, retail sentiment around NVS stock stayed within the ‘bearish’ territory over the past 24 hours, while message volume rose from ‘low’ to ‘normal’ levels.

NVS stock has gained 9% year-to-date.

data.title: Starlink responds to Reliance statement, says "Ready to connect India with high-speed internet"
data.description:
Washington DC, Oct. 16 -- Elon Musk's Starlink on Friday (local time) said it was ready to connect India with high-speed internet, highlighting its work with regulators, industry stakeholders and operators in the country for more than five years.

In a post on X, Starlink said, "We have worked closely with regulators, industry and operators in India for 5+ years, and built a network of dedicated systems, gateways, and other infrastructure all in-country to exclusively serve Indian traffic safely and securely - and all with the requisite government approvals."

"Starlink is ready to connect India with high-speed internet," the company added.

The remarks came in response to Reliance Industries' statement on Friday welcoming competition in India's satellite communications sector, including from Starlink, while stressing that all participants must comply with the country's laws and existing national regulations.

"In light of recent remarks about Reliance and the Indian market, we wish to place the facts on record. Like every Indian enterprise, Reliance has grown in an India that welcomes investment and innovation, homegrown or international, that improve the lives of the people. That openness rests on the rule of law. As the Government of India has stated, it applies the same process to every applicant, Indian or foreign. Jio's own satellite services await clearances," the statements published on X said.

"At Reliance, we have never feared competition. We see it as the truest test of who serves the customer best. Jio itself entered India's crowded telecom market in 2016 as the newest player, with not a single customer. In just ten years, Jio has earned the trust of over 530 million customers and given Indians some of the best digital infrastructure and most affordable data in the world. We welcome competition in satellite communications, including Starlink. Every player, Jio included, must serve the people of India and abide by the laws and policies of the land," the statement added.

The response from Reliance came after SpaceX Chief Executive Officer Elon Musk targeted the Indian conglomerate, alleging that vested interests were blocking Starlink's entry into the sphere.

In a post on X, Musk had said, "The ridiculous arguments by Ambani's army of Internet shills make no sense. On the one hand, they say Starlink couldn't possibly compete with the amazing low prices offered by Ambani's de facto monopoly in India and then, in the same breath, they essentially claim that Starlink would be too strong of a competitor! This is absurd hypocrisy and hyperbole."

He claimed that greater competition could reduce the profits of existing players but said it would not necessarily threaten their business.

"The reality is that competition would greatly benefit the average citizen in India by giving them more choices, as it always does. Ambani's profits will be lower, but he is not going out of business," he said.

Musk had earlier alleged monopolistic practices in the Indian telecommunications landscape and questioned regulatory barriers faced by Starlink's commercial rollout.

"Dear Prime Minister Ambani, Please accept my humble apologies for not realizing that you are the real boss of India. Naturally, you would prefer to maintain your monopolistic exploitation of the great people of India, but would you nonetheless consider allowing Starlink to compete?" Musk posted.

Meanwhile, Union Communications Minister Jyotiraditya Scindia said that there was no question of allowing any monopoly in satellite communications and that three parties are in line for final approval for commercial licences.

Scindia said India is close to a final decision on the pricing framework for satellite communication services, and that all licensed operators, including Starlink, must meet security requirements before commercial operations begin.

data.title: Basis flat, futures slide to three-month low
data.description:
Basis bids for hard red winter wheat were unchanged in the southern US Plains, spot checks showed on Friday, as futures prices tumbled to a three-month low.

  • Rains this week in the southern Plains provided recently planted crops ample moisture for germination, forecasters said.

  • Drier conditions over the coming week should allow for continued planting progress, which stood at 51% complete as of last Sunday.

  • The US Department of Agriculture is scheduled to issue an update on planting progress in a weekly report on Monday.

  • K.C. December hard red winter wheat (KWZ26) last traded 9 cents lower at $7.04 a bushel. The contract earlier dropped to $7.00-1/2 a bushel, its lowest since July 15.
